stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drag one of the three passive receivers (resistor, capacitor, coil) from the palette onto the empty slot at the bottom of the loop. Close the switch. Watch how the ammeter $A$ and voltmeter $V$ react as you swap between receivers. Try all three at least once.
stages.concept: In DC steady state, each passive receiver behaves differently. A resistor $R$ obeys $U = R \cdot I$. A capacitor $C$ blocks steady current: $I = 0$ and $U = E$. An ideal coil $L$ acts like a short: $U = 0$ and $I = E / r$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Two behaviours to match. First: make the ammeter read exactly $0$ (no steady current). Second: make the voltmeter read exactly $0$ across the receiver. Both targets must be hit — swap the receiver as needed.
stages.concept: Zero current in a closed loop means the receiver blocks charge flow — the capacitor is fully charged and no current passes. Zero voltage across the receiver means the receiver drops nothing — the ideal coil, a short in DC, drops all $E$ across the internal $r$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The receiver inside the black-box slot is unknown. The meter readings shown are the steady-state values measured on the real circuit. From those two numbers alone, pick the passive receiver that matches. One attempt.
stages.concept: Identify the receiver from its DC signature: $I = 0$ and $U = E$ points to a capacitor. $U = 0$ and $I = E/r$ points to a coil. Any other finite $(U, I)$ with $U = R \cdot I$ points to a resistor.

labels.diag_ok_coil: steady state: coil is a short
labels.tip1: drag a receiver into the slot; click the switch to toggle; then swap for another type
labels.tip2: one receiver gives I=0, another gives U=0 — swap until you hit both
labels.tip3: read the meters, decide the type, drop it in — one attempt only
labels.peek_tip: capacitor: $I = 0$, $U = E$. coil: $U = 0$, $I = E/r$. resistor: any other finite $(U, I)$.

1.1: Grab a receiver from the palette on the right and drop it into the empty slot at the bottom of the loop.
1.2: Close the switch by clicking it. Now read the ammeter and voltmeter. Then swap the receiver for a different type and compare.
1.3: You have not yet placed one of the three receiver types. Try the one you haven't used.

2.1: One target says I = 0, the other says U = 0. Different receivers give different signatures.
2.2: A capacitor in DC steady state carries no current. An ideal coil in DC steady state drops no voltage.
2.3: Place a capacitor to satisfy the I = 0 target. Place a coil to satisfy the U = 0 target.

3.1: Compare the shown meter readings to the DC signatures of each receiver.
3.2: If I is exactly zero and U equals E, only a capacitor fits. If U is zero and I is E/r, only a coil fits.
3.3: Compute R = U / I. If it matches a plausible resistor value, the answer is a resistor. Otherwise use the extreme cases.
